description: We are a student team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are interested in space exploration, STEM, technology, and game development. Our goal is to build an engaging 2D web-based game that allows players to experience the challenges of managing a lunar or Martian outpost. We are looking for motivated teammates interested in programming, game design, UI/UX, research, and creative problem-solving. Teamwork, curiosity, and a willingness to learn are essential.

details: ARES: FIRST COLONY ARES: First Colony is a 2D browser-based educational simulation game in which players take command of humanity’s first Mars outpost. Their mission is to establish and manage a sustainable colony while keeping the crew alive for 30 Martian days. Players build and manage essential facilities, including habitats, greenhouses, solar panels, water-recycling systems, oxygen generators, and radiation shelters. Each facility has specific costs and effects on the colony’s resources. Players must carefully balance oxygen, water, food, energy, and radiation protection while responding to unexpected events such as dust storms, equipment malfunctions, and system failures. Every decision affects the colony’s stability and the crew’s survival. The project aims to make the challenges of space exploration more accessible and engaging, especially for students. Through interactive gameplay, players learn about life-support systems, resource management, sustainable food production, energy generation, and the difficulties of maintaining human life in an extreme environment. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making by allowing players to experience the consequences of their choices in a simplified simulated environment. For development, we use React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS to create a browser-based experience, alongside 2D game assets and simulation logic. The game is designed to run without requiring external APIs during gameplay, ensuring that its core experience remains accessible and reliable. The creative aspect of ARES is the way it combines colony-building gameplay with interconnected scientific and engineering concepts. Instead of presenting space science only through text or static information, the project turns it into a series of practical challenges. For example, a dust storm can reduce solar energy production, affecting water recycling and other life-support systems. This helps players understand how one problem can influence an entire colony. During development, our team considered scientific relevance, educational value, gameplay simplicity, accessibility, and the limited resources available to a Mars mission. We also aimed to distinguish real scientific references from simplified gameplay assumptions, so that the game remains educational without presenting its simulated values as actual NASA measurements. Ultimately, ARES: First Colony seeks to inspire students to explore space science and engineering by giving them the opportunity to experience the complexity, responsibility, and creativity involved in building humanity’s future beyond Earth.
